forecasts.reason: The pixel fraction drops from 0.755 to 0.694, which saves about 0.3-0.45 s at about V=7.5 s. The 32 px tail is untouched, so I expect a loss of about 0.3 pp. That is a far milder trade than E011, and the tip's 0.77 pp margin absorbs it.

Trimming 0.75 epoch at 24 px costs only about 0.33 s of the cheapest compute. The stretched schedule keeps the 32 px phase intact, so the loss should be about 0.2-0.3 pp. The per-second saving is about the same as I023.

With a fresh cache, max-autotune benchmarks kernels by timing and may pick different ones, so accuracy is not guaranteed to be bit-identical. I expect the held-out seeds to shrink the 3-seed margin by about 0.1-0.3 pp.

Going from 238 to about 380 steps adds per-step Muon Newton-Schulz, Lookahead and kernel-efficiency costs, about +7%. Accuracy probably rises about 0.3-0.6 pp at about 1 s/pp, which beats the epoch price, but the time objective gets worse unless epochs are then cut.
The time cost is zero. The optimizer nudges so far were noise, and the tip's 0.7607 is partly luck, so I expect regression rather than a +0.3 pp gain.
Group 2 is about 50% of conv FLOPs. Narrowing it to 320 cuts total FLOPs about 16%, which should save about 0.4 s. Width costs about 1.6 s/pp, so I expect about -0.5 pp, landing near the bar.

cruxes: How much of the tip's 0.77 pp margin is real? That means the held-out seeds 3-12 offset, and whether E016's +0.33 pp from halving weight decay is signal or a reshuffle. It sets how much low-resolution or epoch trimming is affordable.
Is accuracy set mostly in the 32 px tail? If so, 24 px-phase cuts (I023/I024) are nearly free at about 0.3-0.45 s each and can be stacked.
What is the fixed cost F (upload, whitening, augmentation, interpolation) versus per-step compute? It determines whether trimming FLOPs keeps yielding proportional time savings.

W3 (cost lens), after E016. The tip is 6.58 s at 0.7607 (wd halved). The +0.33 pp over E015 is probably half real: my claim that weight decay only reaches biases and the head may understate its effect through the head.

Budget: time ≈ F (about 0.9 s) + V × pixel fraction, with V about 7.5 s for 9.5 epochs at full resolution and the current pixel fraction 0.755. Systems levers are exhausted (CUDA graphs gave 1%).

The cheapest remaining savings are 24 px compute:
- Dropping the 28 px phase or trimming 24 px epochs costs about 0.3-0.45 s for about 0.2-0.3 pp.
- Narrowing group 2 cuts about 16% of FLOPs for about 0.5 pp.
- A smaller batch is an accuracy lever at about 1 s/pp, cheaper than epochs at 2 s/pp. It could be converted into an epoch cut.

Margin: 0.77 pp on 3 seeds, of which I would treat about 0.4 pp as spendable.
